ai.description: This gecko reaches 55–60 mm SVL. It is brownish-grey with dark dorsal spots and a white venter. Key features include a slender body, smooth ventral scales, and a distinct lack of enlarged tubercles.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Hemidactylus chikhaldaraensis* is best distinguished by the presence of 8–10 longitudinal rows of strongly keeled, trihedral tubercles on its dorsum.
ai.habitat: *Hemidactylus chikhaldaraensis* is endemic to the dry deciduous forests of the Satpura Range, typically found at elevations between 800 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: *Hemidactylus chikhaldaraensis* is primarily nocturnal, actively foraging for small insects on rock surfaces and tree trunks under the cover of darkness.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hemidactylus chikhaldaraensis* is oviparous, laying a clutch of two hard-shelled eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically from June to September.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Hemidactylus chikhaldaraensis* is endemic to the Satpura Range in Maharashtra, India, specifically inhabiting the Chikhaldara plateau at elevations around 1,100 meters.
